headline: Social Media Detox: How to Do One, What to Expect and a 7-Day Plan
description: Thinking of a social media break? Here is how to do a social media detox, what to expect, what the research says and a simple 7-day plan to start now.

itemListElement.name: Social Media Detox: How to Do One, What to Expect and a 7-Day Plan

mainEntity.name: What is a social media detox?

acceptedAnswer.text: A deliberate, time-limited break from social media, from a weekend to several weeks. You choose which platforms to drop, how long to stay away and what to do instead.

mainEntity.name: How long should a social media detox last?

acceptedAnswer.text: No ideal length has been established. Experiments tested one to six weeks, and one week produced measurable differences in the Bath trial, so seven days is a sensible start.

mainEntity.name: What are the benefits of quitting social media?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the experiments above, people reported modest gains in well-being, and some reported less depression, anxiety or loneliness, plus more offline time. Results vary, and you may also lose some news knowledge or contact.

mainEntity.name: What happens to your brain and mood when you quit social media?

acceptedAnswer.text: The studies measured self-reported mood, loneliness and time use, not brain activity. Many people feel restless at first; some then feel calmer, while others notice little change.

mainEntity.name: How do I do a detox without losing touch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell close contacts how to reach you by text or call, move key group chats to a messaging app and message people directly during the week.

mainEntity.name: Should I deactivate my accounts or just delete the apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting the apps is the gentler first step, but log out as well because the browser still works. Deactivating is a firmer break. Choose based on how easily you slip back.

mainEntity.name: How do I come back without relapsing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Return to one platform at a time, keep apps off your home screen, set a timer, turn off notifications and review how you feel after two weeks.
